title: Mock 4 · Compliance Desk
blurb: Think like a compliance officer: reporting, ad approvals, CSCRF categories and SEBI's penalty lessons.

questions.q: Why does the proposal call for separate branding of the new asset class?
options: To differentiate it from traditional MFs and protect existing MF schemes' reputation from its risks and underperformance
To market it only to non-resident investors
To let AMCs charge higher exit loads
questions.explanation: Branding is meant to differentiate the new asset class from traditional MFs and protect the reputation of existing MF schemes from its potential risks and underperformance.
hints: It is regulated; branding does not avoid registration.
Correct: differentiation and reputation protection.
No NRI-only marketing is mentioned.
Exit loads are not the reason given.

questions.q: When were REITs introduced by SEBI, and when was the first REIT launched in India?
options: Introduced in 2014; first REIT launched in 2014
Introduced in 2019; first REIT launched in 2021
Introduced in 2014; first REIT launched in 2019
Introduced in 2007; first REIT launched in 2014
questions.explanation: REITs in India were introduced by SEBI in 2014, and the first REIT was launched in 2019.
hints: The first launch came five years after introduction.
2019 is the launch year, not the introduction year.
Correct: 2014 and 2019.
2007 is not mentioned; 2014 is the introduction year.

questions.q: What range of dividend yields have Indian InvITs delivered so far, according to the deck?
questions.explanation: InvITs provide regular income with dividend yields in the range of 8 to 10% p.a. so far.
hints: Correct: 8-10% for InvITs.
15-18% is not mentioned.
6-8% is the REIT range.
3-5% is too low.

questions.q: Which purchase-date cut-off is relevant to the post-Budget 2024 capital gains structure?
questions.explanation: Under 'Purchase date' the deck lists: before April 1, 2024 and on or after April 1, 2024. July 23, 2024 is the sell-date cut-off.
hints: January 31, 2018 is not mentioned in the deck.
July 23, 2024 is the SELL-date cut-off.
April 1, 2001 is not mentioned in the deck.
Correct: April 1, 2024.

questions.q: Which investor categories does the deck identify as affecting the capital gains tax structure?
questions.explanation: Under 'Investor category' the deck lists resident Indian, non-resident and non-individual.
hints: Employment type is not listed.
Gender/age is not listed.
Correct: resident, non-resident, non-individual.
These are SEBI-style investor classes, not the tax categories listed.

questions.q: Within how many days must the half-yearly periodic report be submitted to BSE?
questions.explanation: The periodic report is to be submitted on a half-yearly basis within 7 working days.
hints: Correct: 7 working days.
21 calendar days is the grievance redressal timeline.
30 days is not the reporting deadline.
15 working days is not the deadline.

questions.q: On SCORES, where does the Action Taken Report (ATR) uploaded by the IA go?
options: It is sent only to NISM
It is kept confidential and never shown to the investor
It is printed and posted to SEBI Bhavan
It is automatically routed to the investor who filed the complaint
questions.explanation: The ATR is automatically routed to the investor who filed the complaint.
hints: NISM has no role.
The investor sees the ATR.
The process is online.
Correct: auto-routed to the complainant.

questions.q: From July 25, 2024, where must a person apply for registration as an investment adviser?
options: To NISM along with the X-A result
To BSE, through its online membership portal
questions.explanation: Applicants desirous of IA/RA registration submit their application to the Exchange (BSE) w.e.f. July 25, 2024 via the online interface at membershipraia.bseindia.com.
hints: NISM does not process registrations.
Correct: via BSE's online portal.
An ARN is for MF distributors, not IAs.
Applications now go through BSE, not by post to SEBI.

questions.q: A complaint is pending on SCORES and the complainant opts for Online Dispute Resolution. What happens to the SCORES complaint?
options: It is treated as disposed on SCORES
It stays open until the ODR award is enforced
It is transferred to the RBI Ombudsman
The complainant must withdraw ODR first
questions.explanation: If the complainant opts for ODR or other civil remedies while the complaint is pending on SCORES, it is treated as disposed on SCORES.
hints: Correct: it is treated as disposed.
It does not remain open in parallel.
RBI Ombudsman is not involved.
Investors can approach ODR at any point.

questions.q: Annexure B must be submitted with an advertisement approval application when:
options: The ad is for print media
The ad is in a regional language
The advertisement has individuals forming part of it
questions.explanation: Annexure B is required if the advertisement has any individuals forming part of it.
hints: The IA's legal form is not the trigger.
Medium does not trigger Annexure B.
Language does not trigger Annexure B.
Correct: when individuals appear in the ad.

questions.q: How does BSE treat an advertisement issued by an Associated Person of an IA on their own?
options: It shall not be entertained by BSE
questions.explanation: Any advertisement issued by an Associated Person on their own shall not be entertained by BSE.
hints: There is no automatic approval.
Annexure A does not change this.
Correct: BSE will not entertain it.
It is not in the exempt list.

questions.q: Under the social-media obligations, an employee who receives market-related news may forward it only:
options: After it has been seen and approved by the IA's Compliance Officer
After verifying it with two friends
If it comes from a WhatsApp group of brokers
questions.explanation: Employees should forward market-related news only after it has been seen and approved by the IA's Compliance Officer; otherwise they are liable for action.
hints: Client consent is not the test.
Correct: Compliance Officer approval first.
Informal verification is not enough.
The source does not exempt it.

questions.q: The SEBI circular on display of IA details (name, registration number, Compliance Officer and grievance contacts, disclaimer) became effective from:
questions.explanation: The circular dated April 06, 2023 has an effective date of May 01, 2023.
hints: July 31, 2024 is the BSE Master Circular date.
Correct: effective May 01, 2023.
March 15, 2024 is for the BSE approval number.
April 06, 2023 is the circular date, not the effective date.

questions.q: Within what time must a Small-size RE report a cyber incident under CSCRF?
questions.explanation: Self-certification, Small and Mid-size REs report within 24 hours of detection; Qualified REs within 6 hours.
hints: 7 days is far too late.
1 month is a report-submission timeline for VAPT/audit.
6 hours applies to Qualified REs.
Correct: 24 hours.

questions.q: Which of these entities is excluded from submission of compliance under CSCRF?
questions.explanation: Excluded REs include FPIs, FVCIs, LPCC, QDPs, REITs/InvITs and Vault Managers.
hints: A ₹5,000 crore PMS is a Mid-size RE.
Brokers are categorised by active clients.
Correct: REITs/InvITs are excluded.
MFs are categorised by AUM.

questions.q: Which of these is placed ONLY in the Self-certification category under CSCRF?
questions.explanation: Only-self-certified REs: Collective Investment Schemes, Credit Rating Agencies and Debenture Trustees (subject to conditions).
hints: Correct: CRAs are self-certification REs.
DPs are Mid or Qualified by type.
MFs are Small, Mid or Qualified by AUM.
Stock exchanges are MIIs.

questions.q: For Small-size and Self-certification REs that have no IT Committee, who reviews and approves CSCRF compliance?
questions.explanation: In the absence of an IT Committee, compliance to CSCRF is reviewed and approved by the MD/CEO/Board member/Partners/Proprietor.
hints: The statutory auditor is not the approver.
Correct: top management or the proprietor.
CERT-In does not approve RE compliance.
BSE does not approve internal compliance.

questions.q: Under the PIT Regulations code, what is the 'restricted list' maintained by the compliance officer used for?
options: Approving or rejecting applications for pre-clearance of trades
questions.explanation: The compliance officer confidentially maintains a 'restricted list' of securities used as the basis for approving or rejecting pre-clearance of trades.
hints: It is not about certifications.
It is not about advertisements.
Correct: it governs pre-clearance of trades.
Complaint lists are separate.

questions.q: According to the Investor Charter, an IA must maintain records of interactions with:
options: Only clients who pay above ₹1 lakh
All clients, including prospective clients before onboarding, where advice-related conversation took place
questions.explanation: The charter requires maintaining records of interactions with all clients including prospective clients (prior to onboarding) where any advice-related conversation took place.
hints: It applies to all clients, not just complainants.
There is no fee threshold.
It applies to all clients.
Correct: including prospects where advice was discussed.

questions.q: In one SEBI order, collecting GST from clients without having GST registration was treated as:
options: Permissible if disclosed in the agreement
questions.explanation: Case 2 lists 'Collection of GST from clients during FY 2018-19 and 2019-20 without having GST registration - Fraudulent Activity'.
hints: Correct: it was called fraudulent.
It was not treated as minor.
No such exemption exists.
Disclosure does not make it legal.

questions.q: With which agency did an IA fail to register for CKYC, leading to a SEBI penalty?
questions.explanation: Case 4: the Noticee failed to register with the CKYC agency CERSAI and maintain KYC records.
hints: NISM is a certification body.
NSDL e-Gov is not the CKYC agency named.
CVL is a KRA, not the CKYC agency named.
Correct: CERSAI runs the Central KYC Registry.

questions.q: In the study cited, investors who reviewed their portfolio monthly ended up with roughly what equity allocation, compared with 70% for those who reviewed yearly?
questions.explanation: Portfolio reviewed yearly: 70% stocks/30% bonds; reviewed monthly: 41% stocks/59% bonds, showing frequent evaluation leads to conservative portfolios.
hints: 59% is the bond share for monthly reviewers.
30% is the yearly reviewers' bond share.
Correct: 41% stocks.
70% is the yearly reviewers' equity share.

questions.q: An investor values the shares he owns far above what he would pay to buy them today. This is:
questions.explanation: Ownership bias, sometimes called the endowment effect, is the tendency to place a higher value on a position than others would, causing investors to hold positions they would not buy now.
hints: Correct: ownership bias.
Gambler's fallacy is predicting random events from past outcomes.
Recency bias overweights recent results.
Herding is following others.

questions.q: Which strategy combines strategic asset allocation with dynamic strategies, adjusting the mix to the client's evolving goals and market conditions?
questions.explanation: Integrated asset allocation is a combination of SAA and dynamic strategies that adjusts based on evolving goals and market conditions.
hints: Buy-and-hold is not the described combination.
Correct: integrated asset allocation.
Insured protects a minimum value.
Drifting lets weights move without adjustment.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the two tests for a long-term portfolio mentioned in the module?
options: The investor can and will live with it
It beats the Nifty 50 every year
It has the lowest possible fees
questions.explanation: Tests: (1) the investor can and will live with it; (2) its long-term reasonably expectable results will meet the investor's own priorities.
hints: Correct: the investor can and will live with it.
Beating an index every year is not a test.
Low fees matter but are not one of the two tests.
A stock count is not a test.
